issues.detail: Compatibility description claims Python examples are provided, but only JavaScript and JSON examples appear in the Instructions and Examples sections.

scenarios.name: elasticsearch-product-index
scenarios.rationale: Response A fully satisfies all six rubric requirements: custom analyzer with edge_ngram, explicit search_analyzer without edge_ngram, text/keyword/numeric mappings, and a completion field for autocomplete. Response B omits the completion field entirely (using edge_ngram multi-fields instead) and lacks an explicitly defined search_analyzer in settings, failing two critical requirements, though it offers broader architectural alternatives.

scenarios.name: incremental-database-sync
scenarios.rationale: Both cover all rubric requirements (timestamp queries, ID-based idempotency, soft-delete removal, failure logging), but Response A provides more complete production guidance (class-based structure, explicit batch sizing, SQL schema setup, stronger delete error handling) while Response B offers simpler code with incremental improvements noted separately; Response A's error isolation is more robust for the use case.

scenarios.name: search-api-and-ranking
scenarios.rationale: Response A provides a complete MongoDB implementation but uses text search instead of multi_match with field boosting, MongoDB filters instead of bool clauses, and $group aggregations instead of ES aggs—misaligning with all four rubric specifics. Response B uses Elasticsearch throughout, implementing multi_match with name^5 boosting exactly as specified, bool filters for category/price ranges, ES aggregations for facets, and zero-result query analysis with synonym pair examples in the mapping.
